questions.q: Why would an admin build a custom report type instead of using a standard one?
options: Standard report types can't be scheduled
A standard type doesn't expose the object, relationship, or field combination a report needs
Custom report types run faster than standard ones
Standard report types can only be used in Classic
questions.explain: Standard report types are fixed combinations Salesforce ships. Custom report types exist for everything those combinations don't cover, including custom objects and uncovered relationships.

questions.q: Once a custom report type is saved, what can no longer be changed?
options: The category
The field layout
The primary object
The display label
questions.explain: The primary object is locked in after the first save. Labels, categories, related objects, and field layout can all still be edited.

questions.q: Which relationship setting is required to report on accounts that have zero opportunities?
options: Each "A" must have a related "B"
"A" records may or may not have a related "B"
Either setting works the same way
Neither; this requires a formula field
questions.explain: "May or may not have" behaves like a left join, keeping parent records even when no related record exists. "Must have" behaves like an inner join and would exclude exactly the accounts the manager wants to see.

questions.q: What does setting a custom report type's status to "In Development" do?
options: It deletes the report type after 30 days
It hides the type and its reports from everyone except users with Manage Custom Report Types
It prevents the report type from ever being deployed
It restricts the type to Salesforce Classic only
questions.explain: In Development is a testing state: only admins with the Manage Custom Report Types permission can see or run reports on it. Deployed makes it available to anyone with access.

questions.q: What does the Edit Layout screen on a custom report type control?
options: Which fields are available to every report built on that report type
The color scheme of reports using that type
Which users can run the report type
The report's default chart type
questions.explain: Edit Layout sets the ceiling on available fields and sections for any report built on the type — it doesn't touch user access, which is controlled separately through folder sharing and permissions.
